newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Regent Pacific seen in US$50 mln float - sources.
newsitem.headline: Regent Pacific seen in US$50 mln float - sources.

text.p: Global emerging markets investment house Regent Pacific Group Ltd is expected to raise about US$50 million in a share flotation, market sources said on Monday.
The company is expected to issue 170.5 million new shares at a price ranging from HK$2.30 to HK$2.70 per share, representing a prospective price/earnings multiple of 8.00 to 10.4 times, sources said.

"About 75 percent of the issue is expected to be placed internationally and 25 percent going to an IPO (initial public offering) in Hong Kong," said an analyst after attending a company presentation on Monday.
The IPO is expected to run from May 6 to 9 and dealing in the shares is expected to begin on May 19, sources said.
Nomura International Hong Kong Ltd is expected to be the sponsor of the issue, they said.

The net proceeds from the issue is expected to be used to expand its business in the United States, to establish a new fund management group, to acquire a financial house in Europe, and to further expand into emerging markets, sources said.
The Regent Pacific Group, headquartered in Hong Kong, provides investment management and advisory services in emerging markets to institutional and professional investors wordwide.
The group said in a separate statement on Monday that it managed and advised 43 funds with about US$1.77 billion worth of assets under management as at February 1997.
Its core activities concentrate on fund management, corporate finance, corporate investment, and European securities.
The company said its turnover increased to US$37.6 million for the year ended in March 1996, from US$34.4 million in 1995 and US$17.5 million in 1994.

About 32.8 percent of revenues came from annual management/investment advisory fees, 11.7 percent from performance fees, 5.2 percent from brokerage rebate commissions, 9.8 percent from launch/arrangement fees, 2.2 percent from Russian brokerage and 38.3 percent from corporate investments, the statement said.

The group said its operating profit rose to US$23.7 million in 1996, from US$22.5 million in 1995 and US$11.1 million in 1994. Profit attributable to shareholders was at US$21.5 million in 1996, compared with US$22.3 million in 1995 and US$11.2 million in 1994.
